chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Talaqani (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Abu Sa'id al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Adawi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Tamim narrated to us from al-Hasan ibn Abd al-Rahman from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman from al-Hakam ibn Utayba from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla from his father. He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

No servant will have believed until I am more beloved to him than himself, and my family is more beloved to him than his family, and my progeny is more beloved to him than his progeny, and my essence is more beloved to him than his essence.
He said: Then a man from the community said: O Abu Abd al-Rahman! You never cease bringing hadiths by which God enlivens the hearts.

key_terms.أهلي: My family (ahli) - the Prophet's household, the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.ذاتي: My essence/person (dhati) - the Prophet's very being and personality
key_terms.عترتي: My progeny (itra) - the Prophet's descendants through Fatima and Ali, a term central to Shia theology as it designates the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.يحيي الله به القلوب: By which God enlivens the hearts - indicates the spiritual revivification that comes from hearing prophetic traditions about love

ai.seo_question: What does the Prophet say about loving his family and progeny as a condition of faith?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) declares that true faith requires loving him more than oneself, and loving his family (ahl), progeny (itra), and very essence (dhat) more than one's own. This hadith goes beyond the well-known Sunni version (which only mentions loving the Prophet more than oneself) by explicitly extending this requirement to the Prophet's family and progeny — a distinctive Shia emphasis that connects love of the Prophet to love of the Ahl al-Bayt. The closing remark from a listener, praising the narrator for bringing hadiths that 'enliven the hearts,' reflects the emotional impact such traditions had on early Muslim audiences.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq al-Talaqani (ra) narrated to us. He said: Abu Sa`id al-Hasan b. `Ali al-`Adawi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Tamim narrated to us from al-Hasan b. `Abd al-Rahman from Muhammad b. `Abd al-Rahman from al-Hakam b. `Atiyya from `Abd al-Rahman b. Abi Layla from his father. He said: The Messenger of Allah (s) said:

No worshiper will have believed until I am more beloved to him than himself, and my family is more beloved to him than his family, and my progeny is more beloved to him than his progeny, and my essence is more beloved to him than his essence.
He said: So, a man from the community said: O Aba `Abd al-Rahman! You did not stop from bringing this hadith by which Allah has enlivened our hearts.
